title: The Rivergate of Devil's Throat
premise: Lena Winterbourne, a salvage diver drowning in debt, takes a job recovering a navy-blacklisted wreck in Devil's Throat gorge, guided only by her late father's compass. When the expedition upriver goes silent, she learns the wreck holds a manifest that could expose the salvage fleet's owner—her employer, Aldous Crane—as a war profiteer who sank his own ships. Racing the fleet by six tides, Lena must decide whether to sell the truth for her freedom or burn her only escape by revealing it. In the end, she broadcasts the manifest from the wreck itself, sacrificing the salvage payout but claiming her father's name and her own.
about_author: Astrid Fairweather is a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade charting river deltas before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels from a houseboat on the northern coast, drawing on real wrecks and the people who can't leave them alone.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Broke and hounded by creditors, Lena accepts a salvage contract from Aldous Crane to reach a wreck in Devil's Throat before his own fleet does—six tides of head start, no questions allowed. The chapter establishes her debt, her father's compass, and her instinct for invisibility. Emotional beat: desperate hope laced with unease at Crane's evasiveness.

chapters.title: The Silent Upriver
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Loading the expedition at Rivergate, Lena notices the advance team's radio has gone dead for three days and their last transmission cut mid-word. Crane dismisses her concerns and doubles her fee to keep her moving. Emotional beat: creeping dread as she realizes she's being paid not to think.

chapters.title: Gorge Water
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, with a brief interlude from deckhand Tomas. The crew enters Devil's Throat—sheer cliffs, whirlpools, and a current that fights the boat every fathom. They find the advance team's abandoned raft snagged on rocks, bloodied but empty. Tomas quietly warns Lena that Crane's fleet is closer behind than promised. Emotional beat: isolation tightening into fear.

chapters.title: What the Compass Wants
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Her father's compass stops pointing north and swings toward the gorge wall, leading her to a flooded side-cavern and the first wreck—decades older than the navy file claims, its hold stamped with Crane Shipping marks. She realizes the 'one wreck' is a lie. Emotional beat: the shock of recognizing her employer in the crime scene.

chapters.title: The Man in the Water
chapters.summary: Alternating Lena and Tomas POV. They pull a survivor from the advance team—half-drowned engineer Ruth Okafor, who reveals the team found the manifest and Crane ordered them silenced. Ruth's loyalty to Crane curdles into testimony. That night, fleet spotter planes pass overhead. Emotional beat: betrayal made personal; the crew must choose sides.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas, who owes Crane his brother's medical debts, wrestles with Ruth's accusations and secretly radios the fleet—then hears Crane order the gorge 'sealed' with the expedition inside it. Horrified, he confesses to Lena. Emotional beat: guilt, and the first true alliance built on honesty rather than wages.

chapters.title: The Second Wreck
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Diving deeper than safe limits, Lena finds the primary wreck and the manifest: Crane scuttled his own ships with crew aboard to collect insurance and hide arms shipments. Her compass belonged to her father, one of the 'lost' crew. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused—this wreck is her inheritance.

chapters.title: Fleet at the Throat
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Crane's salvage fleet blocks the gorge mouth, and his enforcer offers Lena a fortune for the manifest and silence—her debts erased, her father's compass returned 'as a courtesy.' She stalls, buying a tide. Ruth and Tomas rig the boat for a night run through the whirlpools. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The climax: a running battle through the gorge as the fleet closes in. Lena dives the wreck one last time to rig the manifest to a salvage buoy and triggers the emergency beacon, broadcasting the documents to every receiver on the coast as Crane's men breach the cavern. The compass, wedged in her father's wreck, stays behind. Emotional beat: letting go of survival-by-invisibility at last.

chapters.title: Rivergate
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, epilogue tone. Crane's empire cracks under the broadcast; Lena surfaces to a coast full of listening radios and a fleet in retreat. Debt collectors scatter, Ruth and Tomas stand with her, and she takes work as an independent diver—her name, not a pen name, on the contract. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won freedom; identity claimed.
